title: Champions vs native Ascend aclnn (CANN 9.0.0), measured 2026-11-07

protocol.pypto_side: frozen remote_harness.py (sha256 5c7b7aa4... identical across all domain verifiers and /root/ptocontri/pkg), latency_us = median per-round effective_us (PYPTO_BENCH=1)
protocol.aclnn_side: tools/aclnn_bench.py (pyacl + ctypes on libopapi.so): wall-clock per round (enqueue aclnn call(s) + acl.rt.synchronize_stream), median; aclnn executor fetched once via *GetWorkspaceSize, marked repeatable, reused across rounds. Both sides are end-to-end wall clock including host dispatch.
protocol.shape_policy: primary = champion's native decision preset {M:512, N:1024, bf16} (s-tier campaign); secondary = m-tier {M:4096, N:4096} for cross-op comparability

aclnn_baseline_semantics: Our kernel takes (x, dy, gamma) and produces dx/dgamma/dbeta in ONE call, recomputing forward stats (mean, rstd) internally. aclnnLayerNormBackward requires mean/rstd as INPUTS, so the apples-to-apples baseline for a user holding only (x, dy, gamma) is aclnnLayerNorm (stats-producing forward pass) + aclnnLayerNormBackward(outputMask=[1,1,1]). Constraints found on-machine: gamma must be 1-D [N]; mean/rstd outputs must be [M,1] fp32; dgamma/dbeta must be 1-D [N] fp32 ([1,N] is silently accepted but returns NaN garbage — probed and rejected). eps=1e-5 matches our contract.

results.note: at its native s-tier preset the fused single-call kernel is 2.45x faster than the native two-call composition (and aclnnLayerNormBackward alone cannot even run without a stats-producing pass).

OUT-OF-CAMPAIGN shape: e000037 is an s-tier champion (resident/atomic small-row design); at 4096x4096 it dispatches to its generic streamed path and is 2.6x slower than aclnn. Recorded as-is for comparability; not the campaign's claimed operating point.

convention: speedup_pypto_vs_aclnn = aclnn_us / pypto_us; >1 means the pypto champion is faster
